open_gaps.reason: actix.scope_route.v1 joins a scope prefix to routes only when the routes chain directly off `web::scope("/lit")` in the same expression. Routes registered under a scope via `.configure(fn)` or `.service(handler)` live in a cross-file target, so their scope prefix cannot flow into their effective_route_template in-file; actix.mount.v1 records the prefix at the scope site with mount_path/mount_target only.
open_gaps.required_closure: resolve the scope prefix to routes registered in a cross-file configure/service target, which is Miller's cross-file join responsibility per decision 0004; the extractor emits actix.mount.v1 and guesses no join

open_gaps.reason: actix.scope_route.v1 reads the scope prefix by walking the `.route` receiver chain to a base `web::scope(literal)` in the same expression. A scope bound to a variable first (`let s = web::scope("/api"); s.route(...)`) is cross-statement single-assignment tracing, which is not attempted this slice; such routes stay silent (M2) rather than emit a route with an unresolved prefix.
open_gaps.required_closure: add same-file single-assignment receiver tracing for scope variables (the axum receiver-poison model applied to `web::scope`), fixture-backed

open_gaps.reason: actix `web::resource("/x").route(web::get().to(h))` and guard-based route forms register routes without a `web::scope` prefix chain, so they are not covered by actix.scope_route.v1 (which anchors on scope prefixes) and stay silent.
open_gaps.required_closure: add a `web::resource`/route-guard collector emitting a resource route fact with the resource path and method-router verb, fixture-backed

open_gaps.reason: axum route params are recorded as brace captures (`{id}`, axum 0.8). axum 0.7 used `:id`; the extractor cannot know the crate version and does not version-sniff (design section 11), so a 0.7 `:id` template passes through to a correct normalized_route_template join key but its `:id` segment is not recorded in dynamic_segments.
open_gaps.required_closure: no closure without version detection, which is explicitly out of scope; a 0.7 `:id` template still joins correctly, only dynamic_segments under-reports its params

open_gaps.reason: A `.nest("/api", sub_router)` mounts a sub-router whose routes are defined in another function/file, so the nest prefix cannot flow into those routes' effective_route_template in-file; axum.nest.v1 records the mount at its own site with mount_path/mount_target only.
open_gaps.required_closure: resolve nest prefix to sub-router routes, which is Miller's cross-file join responsibility per decision 0004; the extractor emits axum.nest.v1 and guesses no join

open_gaps.reason: The reqwest builder form (`client.get("url")`) requires a same-file-proven reqwest receiver (inline `reqwest::Client::new()` chain, a single-assigned local, or a `reqwest::Client` typed param) — a struct-field or cross-file client (`self.client.get(...)`) is syntactically identical to a non-HTTP `.get(...)` and stays silent by M2 (a false client edge is worse than a miss).
open_gaps.required_closure: extend reqwest builder detection to struct-field/typed receivers if in-file type resolution becomes available; scoped `reqwest::get("url")` and proven-receiver forms already emit

CSS has no static type system. Custom property values are runtime strings; there is no type metadata to extract.

open_gaps.reason: Django `re_path` now normalizes common named capture groups such as `(?P<id>...)`, but arbitrary regex constructs such as alternation, optional path fragments, lookaround, and unnamed captures cannot be losslessly converted into a route-template join key. Those facts may emit without `normalized_route_template` rather than guessing.
open_gaps.required_closure: define and fixture a conservative regex-to-route-template normalization policy for additional Django regex constructs, or keep emitting only raw route patterns for non-template-shaped regexes

open_gaps.reason: A RouteServiceProvider `/api` group prefix is applied cross-file (in the provider, not the routes file), so it cannot flow into a route's effective_route_template in-file; route_template is therefore not guaranteed to be the absolute public path when such a prefix applies.
open_gaps.required_closure: resolve RouteServiceProvider group prefixes cross-file, which is Miller's join responsibility per decision 0004; the extractor emits laravel.route_prefix.v1 only for same-file prefixes

open_gaps.reason: Guzzle and Symfony variable receivers are proven only via a typed parameter (`Client`/`ClientInterface`/`HttpClientInterface`/`HttpClient`) or a same-scope `new \GuzzleHttp\Client()` / `HttpClient::create()` assignment — a property (`$this->client->get(...)`) or cross-file/DI-provided receiver is syntactically identical to a non-HTTP call and stays silent by M2 (a false client edge is worse than a miss). Cross-function curl handles also stay silent.
open_gaps.required_closure: extend receiver proofs to promoted-property/class-property receivers if in-file type resolution becomes available; typed-param and same-scope construction forms already emit

open_gaps.reason: The RouterFunction / coRouter functional DSL nests routes via nest()/path() closures that are not single-assignment same-file; annotation routing is the shipped Kotlin+Spring claim.
open_gaps.required_closure: add a lexical-containment collector for coRouter/RouterFunction nesting once a same-file nesting model is designed

open_gaps.reason: Ktor/WebClient/RestTemplate receivers are proven only via a typed function or primary-constructor parameter, an exact `WebClient.create()`/`RestTemplate` builder chain, or (Ktor) a same-file `HttpClient(...)` local — class-property, DI-provided, or cross-file receivers are syntactically identical to non-HTTP fluent calls and stay silent by M2. Retrofit `@HTTP(method = ...)` annotations also stay silent (no static verb element support).
open_gaps.required_closure: extend receiver proofs to class-property/field receivers if in-file type resolution becomes available; add `@HTTP` static-element parsing if demanded

open_gaps.reason: The Phoenix lane emits route/resource/forward facts only; the `pipe_through`, `live` (LiveView), `socket`, and `channel` router macros carry no request→handler HTTP boundary path literal in the same shape, so they emit nothing.
open_gaps.required_closure: add collectors for the LiveView (`live`) and socket/channel surfaces if a live-route or websocket boundary lane is opened; `pipe_through` references a pipeline, not a route, and stays evidence-only

open_gaps.reason: A `scope` prefix declared in another router module (or via a forwarded plug's own router) is applied cross-file, so it cannot flow into a route's effective_route_template in-file; route_template is therefore not guaranteed to be the absolute public path when such a prefix applies.
open_gaps.required_closure: resolve cross-file scope/forward prefixes, which is Miller's join responsibility per decision 0004; the extractor emits phoenix.forward.v1 only for same-file forwards

open_gaps.reason: Tesla client middleware base URLs (`Tesla.client([{Tesla.Middleware.BaseUrl, "https://api"}])`) are declared apart from the request call, so `Tesla.get(client, "/path")` emits only the static path argument — the middleware base URL is not joined into target_path in-file.
open_gaps.required_closure: join same-file Tesla middleware base URLs into request facts if a same-file client-binding model is designed; static URL arguments already emit

open_gaps.reason: Module receivers are matched by literal alias name (`Req.`, `Tesla.`, ...), not resolved through `alias` declarations: `alias MyApp.Fake, as: Req` makes a non-HTTP `Req.get(...)` emit, and `alias Req, as: R` makes real `R.get(...)` calls stay silent.
open_gaps.required_closure: resolve `alias ... , as:` declarations to canonical module names before matching, if in-file alias resolution is added to the Elixir lane

reference_resolution._comment: Documentation mirror of the schema-v4 reference-resolution capability posture. The MACHINE-ENFORCED honesty surfaces are (1) the per-language language_capability_gaps rows emitted at scan time by crates/julie-extract-cli/src/capability_snapshot.rs (reference_resolution.tier2_import / .tier3_receiver / .tier3_static_type) and (2) the fixture suite crates/julie-extract-cli/tests/resolution_contract.rs over fixtures/extraction/resolution_contract/. This block is not deserialized by the extractor (serde ignores unknown fields) and is not read by scripts/language-data-quality-report.mjs; do not add per-language capability_gaps entries for these capabilities here, as the runtime already emits them and their gap_id would collide on the language_capability_gaps primary key. Keep this block in sync with those surfaces and docs/contracts/sqlite-schema-v4.md.
reference_resolution.detection_rule: Consumers gate on the reference_resolution_status metadata key, never on the schema version or table probing.

metadata_keys.reference_resolution_last_full_revision: revision_id of the last full pass; preserved across a failed write

tier1_same_file.confidence_semantics: ceiling capped by source identifier or relationship confidence
tier1_same_file.gating: universal for extraction-native edges; conservative same-file value lookup for variable_ref

tier2_import.gap_reason: import-guided resolution is gated off outside languages with a fixture-tested import contract
tier2_import.required_closure: normalize per-language import facts (module specifier + local binding + imported name) as first-class rows, then enable tier 2

tier3_receiver.gap_reason: receiver-typed resolution coverage is bounded by this language's type_facts emission; the tier ships with measured coverage, not a completeness claim
tier3_receiver.required_closure: broaden type_facts emission (especially for local variables) toward full receiver coverage
tier3_receiver.evidence: fixtures/extraction/resolution_contract/csharp/tier3_receiver (resolves at 0.65 via an inferred field type fact)

tier3_static_type.confidence_semantics: ceiling capped by source identifier or relationship confidence
tier3_static_type.gating: universal, but the tier only yields an edge where the extractor records visibility='public' on the receiver type (for cross-file binding) and static reachability (symbols.metadata_json.isStatic when present, else a standalone 'static' word in the member signature)
tier3_static_type.visibility_dependency: A cross-file receiver is refused unless the type records visibility='public'. Measured emission: rust maps pub and pub(crate) to public, go maps exported to public, python always reports public, javascript reports public on the class symbol, csharp maps internal to private, and typescript records visibility='public' on exported type declarations (export class / export enum / etc.). Non-exported TypeScript types remain non-public so cross-file static binding still refuses. Same-file receivers bind regardless of visibility.
tier3_static_type.visibility_gap_effect: recall loss only, never a wrong edge
tier3_static_type.visibility_required_closure: distinguish C# internal from private, then relax the cross-file refusal to assembly-visible kinds; TypeScript export visibility is fixture-proven for the static tier
tier3_static_type.static_modifier_dependency: A member other than an enum member, constant, or enum binds through a type name only if it is statically reachable, because Type.InstanceMethod() does not compile. Reachability prefers symbols.metadata_json.isStatic when set, then falls back to a standalone 'static' word in the presentation signature. Fixture-proven emission: csharp (signature + isStatic metadata), typescript (exported types + static methods with isStatic and signature 'static'), and javascript (public class + static methods). Remaining gaps: python spells the modifier '@staticmethod', rust associated functions carry no static marker, and other languages lack a fixture-proven contract.
tier3_static_type.static_modifier_gap_effect: recall loss only, never a wrong edge
tier3_static_type.static_modifier_required_closure: emit a language-native static-member marker (a normalized modifier, annotation, or isStatic metadata) for the remaining languages, then register a resolution_contract static_type_receiver fixture and add the language to TIER3_STATIC_TYPE_LANGUAGES
tier3_static_type.per_language_gap_row: reference_resolution.tier3_static_type, emitted at scan time by crates/julie-extract-cli/src/capability_snapshot.rs for every language outside fixture_proven_languages
refuses: receiver type nested inside another type
non-public receiver type referenced outside its declaring file
member that is not statically reachable: isStatic is false or absent and the signature lacks 'static' as a standalone word, and it is not an enum member, constant, or enum
receiver whose written qualification is not a suffix of the candidate type's declared namespace, so External.Fixture never answers for a workspace App.Core.Fixture
receiver shadowed by a parameter of an enclosing callable, which makes the access an instance access on that parameter
tier3_static_type.refusal_reason: type-name uniqueness alone would reproduce the tier-4 wrong-edge failure keyed on type names: a file-scoped workspace type sharing a simple name with an external type would otherwise answer for every same-named reference in the workspace
open_wrong_edge_risks: unqualified reference to a public top-level workspace type whose simple name collides with an external type binds workspace-wide; needs import corroboration

a local variable declaration named exactly like a workspace type shadows it; C# locals/params are now symbols and refuse the static-type path when they bind the receiver name; residual risk remains for languages without local symbols and for untyped `var` bindings without initializer propagation

identifier_context.member_access: receiver is captured in identifiers.metadata_json from the source site or a co-located structured pending target; tier 3 remains type-fact bounded and tier 4 stays disabled
identifier_context.variable_ref: same-file lexical values only; workspace-global value name matching is disabled
